sanskrit: purā rāma mahābāho mahābalaparākrama rūpam āsīn mamācintyaṃ triṣu lokeṣu viśrutam yathā somasya śakrasya sūryasya ca yathā vapuḥ
english: In former times, O Rāma, great-armed one of mighty strength and valor, my form was inconceivable and renowned throughout the three worlds — even as the form of Soma, of Śakra, and of Sūrya.

sanskrit: so 'haṃ rūpam idaṃ kṛtvā lokavitrāsanaṃ mahat ṛṣīn vanagatān rāma trāsayāmi tatas tataḥ
english: That same I, having assumed this form so terrifying to the worlds, went here and there frightening the sages dwelling in the forest, O Rāma.

sanskrit: tataḥ sthūlaśirā nāma maharṣiḥ kopito mayā saṃcinvan vividhaṃ vanyaṃ rūpeṇānena dharṣitaḥ
english: Thereupon a great sage named Sthūlaśiras, while gathering various forest produce, was affronted by me in this form and roused to wrath.

sanskrit: tenāham uktaḥ prekṣyaivaṃ ghoraśāpābhidhāyinā etad eva nṛśaṃsaṃ te rūpam astu vigarhitam
english: He, the utterer of a terrible curse, looked upon me and said: "Let this very cruel and censured form be thine forever."

sanskrit: sa mayā yācitaḥ kruddhaḥ śāpasyānto bhaved iti abhiśāpakṛtasyeti tenedaṃ bhāṣitaṃ vacaḥ
english: I besought him in his fury asking when the curse might end. He who had laid the curse upon me then spoke these words:

sanskrit: yadā chittvā bhujau rāmas tvāṃ dahed vijane vane tadā tvaṃ prāpsyase rūpaṃ svam eva vipulaṃ śubham
english: "When Rāma shall cut off your arms and burn you in a lonely forest, then shall you regain your own expansive and beautiful form."

sanskrit: śriyā virājitaṃ putraṃ danos tvaṃ viddhi lakṣmaṇa indrakopād idaṃ rūpaṃ prāptam evaṃ raṇājire
english: "Know me, O Lakṣmaṇa, to be the radiant and glorious son of Danu — this form was obtained through Indra's wrath on the field of battle, even as I shall relate."

sanskrit: ahaṃ hi tapasogreṇa pitāmaham atoṣayam dīrgham āyuḥ sa me prādāt tato māṃ vibhramo 'spṛśat
english: By fierce austerity I had gratified the Grandfather, and he granted me long life; thereafter a delusion took hold of me.

sanskrit: dīrgham āyur mayā prāptaṃ kiṃ me śakraḥ kariṣyati ity evaṃ buddhim āsthāya raṇe śakram adharṣayam
english: "Long life has been granted to me — what can Śakra do to me?" — resting on this thought, I defied Śakra in battle.

sanskrit: tasya bāhupramuktena vajreṇa śataparvaṇā sakthinī ca śiraś caiva śarīre saṃpraveśitam
english: By the hundred-jointed thunderbolt released from his arm, both my thighs and my head were driven into my body.

sanskrit: sa mayā yācyamānaḥ sann ānayad yamasādanam pitāmahavacaḥ satyaṃ tad astv iti mamābravīt
english: As I implored him, he brought word from the abode of Yama: "Let the word of the Grandfather be true" — thus he spoke to me.

sanskrit: anāhāraḥ kathaṃ śakto bhagnasakthiśiromukhaḥ vajreṇābhihataḥ kālaṃ sudīrgham api jīvitum
english: "Without food, with thighs, head, and mouth smashed and struck by the thunderbolt, how can one live for such a very long time?"

sanskrit: evam uktas tu me śakro bāhū yojanam āyatau prādād āsyaṃ ca me kukṣau tīkṣṇadaṃṣṭram akalpayat
english: Addressed thus by me, Śakra granted arms each a yojana in length, and fashioned a mouth with sharp fangs in my belly.

sanskrit: so 'haṃ bhujābhyāṃ dīrghābhyāṃ samākṛṣya vanecarān siṃhadvipamṛgavyāghrān bhakṣayāmi samantataḥ
english: Thus I, with those two great arms, drag in from all sides forest-wandering creatures — lions, elephants, deer, and tigers — and devour them.

sanskrit: sa tu mām abravīd indro yadā rāmaḥ salakṣmaṇaḥ chetsyate samare bāhū tadā svargaṃ gamiṣyasi
english: And Indra told me: "When Rāma together with Lakṣmaṇa shall sever your arms in battle, then shall you depart for heaven."

sanskrit: sa tvaṃ rāmo 'si bhadraṃ te nāham anyena rāghava śakyo hantuṃ yathātattvam evam uktaṃ maharṣiṇā
english: You are that Rāma — good fortune to you! I cannot be slain by any other, O Rāghava, as the great sage truly declared.

sanskrit: ahaṃ hi matisācivyaṃ kariṣyāmi nararṣabha mitraṃ caivopadekṣyāmi yuvābhyāṃ saṃskṛto 'gninā
english: I shall indeed render counsel to your intelligence, O bull among men, and I shall direct you to a friend — once I am purified by fire at your hands.

sanskrit: evam uktas tu dharmātmā danunā tena rāghavaḥ idaṃ jagāda vacanaṃ lakṣmaṇasyopaśṛṇvataḥ
english: Addressed thus by that son of Danu, the righteous Rāghava spoke this reply while Lakṣmaṇa listened nearby:

sanskrit: rāvaṇena hṛtā sītā mama bhāryā yaśasvinī niṣkrāntasya janasthānāt saha bhrātrā yathāsukham
english: "Sītā, my illustrious wife, has been carried off by Rāvaṇa, freely and at ease, while I had departed from Janasthāna together with my brother.

sanskrit: nāmamātraṃ tu jānāmi na rūpaṃ tasya rakṣasaḥ nivāsaṃ vā prabhāvaṃ vā vayaṃ tasya na vidmahe
english: I know only the name of that rākṣasa, not his form; we know nothing of his dwelling or his power.

sanskrit: śokārtānām anāthānām evaṃ viparidhāvatām kāruṇyaṃ sadṛśaṃ kartum upakāre ca vartatām
english: For us who are grief-stricken and helpless and thus wandering about, it befits one who is compassionate and disposed to render aid.

sanskrit: kāṣṭhāny ānīya śuṣkāṇi kāle bhagnāni kuñjaraiḥ bhakṣyāmas tvāṃ vayaṃ vīra śvabhre mahati kalpite
english: Having gathered dry logs broken in their season by elephants, we shall burn you, O hero, in a great pit that we shall dig.

sanskrit: sa tvaṃ sītāṃ samācakṣva yena vā yatra vā hṛtā kuru kalyāṇam atyarthaṃ yadi jānāsi tattvataḥ
english: You then — tell us of Sītā, by whom or to where she was taken; do us this supreme kindness, if you know the truth."

sanskrit: evam uktas tu rāmeṇa vākyaṃ danur anuttamam provāca kuśalo vaktuṃ vaktāram api rāghavam
english: Addressed thus by Rāma, the son of Danu spoke a most excellent reply — he who was skilled in speech, even to Rāghava who is himself a master of eloquence:

sanskrit: divyam asti na me jñānaṃ nābhijānāmi maithilīm yas tāṃ jñāsyati taṃ vakṣye dagdhaḥ svaṃ rūpam āsthitaḥ
english: "I have no supernatural knowledge, nor do I know of Maithilī. But once I am burned and have regained my own form, I shall tell you of one who will know her.

sanskrit: adagdhasya hi vijñātuṃ śaktir asti na me prabho rākṣasaṃ taṃ mahāvīryaṃ sītā yena hṛtā tava
english: In my unburned state I have no power to discern that rākṣasa of mighty valor, O lord, by whom your Sītā was taken.

sanskrit: vijñānaṃ hi mahad bhraṣṭaṃ śāpadoṣeṇa rāghava svakṛtena mayā prāptaṃ rūpaṃ lokavigarhitam
english: My great knowledge was lost through the fault of the curse, O Rāghava, and this form censured by the world was obtained through my own doing.

sanskrit: kiṃ tu yāvan na yāty astaṃ savitā śrāntavāhanaḥ tāvan mām avaṭe kṣiptvā daha rāma yathāvidhi
english: But before Savitṛ with his weary steeds sets into the west, cast me into the pit and burn me duly, O Rāma.

sanskrit: dagdhas tvayāham avaṭe nyāyena raghunandana vakṣyāmi tam ahaṃ vīra yas taṃ jñāsyati rākṣasaṃ
english: Burned by you in the pit according to the rite, O delight of the Raghu line, I shall tell you, O hero, of the one who will know that rākṣasa.

sanskrit: tena sakhyaṃ ca kartavyaṃ nyāyyavṛttena rāghava kalpayiṣyati te prītaḥ sāhāyyaṃ laghuvikramaḥ
english: And friendship must be made with him — one of righteous conduct, O Rāghava; he of swift valor, being pleased, will render you assistance.

sanskrit: na hi tasyāsty avijñātaṃ triṣu lokeṣu rāghava sarvān parisṛto lokān purā vai kāraṇāntare
english: There is nothing unknown to him in the three worlds, O Rāghava; in former times, for another reason, he ranged through all the worlds."

sanskrit: evam uktau tu tau vīrau kabandhena nareśvarau giripradaram āsādya pāvakaṃ visasarjatuḥ
english: Addressed thus by Kabandha, those two heroes and lords of men, having reached a mountain ravine, kindled fire.

sanskrit: lakṣmaṇas tu maholkābhir jvalitābhiḥ samantataḥ citām ādīpayām āsa sā prajajvāla sarvataḥ
english: Lakṣmaṇa, with blazing firebrands on every side, ignited the pyre, and it flared up all around.

sanskrit: tac charīraṃ kabandhasya ghṛtapiṇḍopamaḥ mahat medasā pacyamānasya mandaṃ dahati pāvaka
english: That great body of Kabandha, like a lump of clarified butter, sizzled slowly as the fire consumed it, rendered down by its own fat.

sanskrit: sa vidhūya citām āśu vidhūmo 'gnir ivotthitaḥ araje vāsasī vibhran mālāṃ divyāṃ mahābalaḥ
english: He quickly shook off the pyre and rose up, like a smokeless fire, wearing spotless garments and a divine garland — that one of great strength.

sanskrit: tataś citāyā vegena bhāsvaro virajāmbaraḥ utpapātāśu saṃhṛṣṭaḥ sarvapratyaṅgabhūṣaṇaḥ
english: Then swiftly from the pyre that radiant one, clad in stainless raiment, leaped up with great joy, adorned with ornaments on every limb.

sanskrit: vimāne bhāsvare tiṣṭhan haṃsayukte yaśaskare prabhayā ca mahātejā diśo daśa virājayan
english: Standing in a luminous celestial chariot yoked with swans and celebrated for glory, that one of great splendor illumined the ten directions with his radiance.

sanskrit: so 'ntarikṣagato rāmaṃ kabandho vākyam abravīt śṛṇu rāghava tattvena yathā sīmām avāpsyasi
english: Kabandha, risen to the sky, spoke to Rāma: "Hear, O Rāghava, truly how you shall reach the boundary of your goal.

sanskrit: rāma ṣaḍ yuktayo loke yābhiḥ sarvaṃ vimṛśyate parimṛṣṭo daśāntena daśābhāgena sevyate
english: O Rāma, there are six expedients in the world by which all is deliberated; one who has been tested by adversity is to be sought in a tenth part of that adversity.

sanskrit: daśābhāgagato hīnas tvaṃ rāma sahalakṣmaṇaḥ yat kṛte vyasanaṃ prāptaṃ tvayā dārapradharṣaṇam
english: You, O Rāma, together with Lakṣmaṇa, are in that diminished tenth-part condition — the calamity of your wife being violated has been brought upon you.

sanskrit: tad avaśyaṃ tvayā kāryaḥ sa suhṛt suhṛdāṃ vara akṛtvā na hi te siddhim ahaṃ paśyāmi cintayan
english: Therefore you must certainly make that ally yours, O best of friends; reflecting on it, I do not see your success without doing so.

sanskrit: śrūyatāṃ rāma vakṣyāmi sugrīvo nāma vānaraḥ bhrātrā nirastaḥ kruddhena vālinā śakrasūnunā
english: Hear, O Rāma, I shall tell you: there is a monkey named Sugrīva, who has been expelled by his angry brother Vālin, son of Śakra.

sanskrit: ṛṣyamūke girivare pampāparyantaśobhite nivasaty ātmavān vīraś caturbhiḥ saha vānaraiḥ
english: That self-possessed hero dwells on the excellent mountain Ṛśyamūka, beautiful with its borders of Pampā, together with four monkeys.

sanskrit: vayasyaṃ taṃ kuru kṣipram ito gatvādya rāghava adrohāya samāgamya dīpyamāne vibhāvasau
english: Go from here this very day and quickly make him your companion, O Rāghava; meet with him without treachery before the blazing fire.

sanskrit: na ca te so 'vamantavyaḥ sugrīvo vānarādhipaḥ kṛtajñaḥ kāmarūpī ca sahāyārthī ca vīryavān
english: Nor should Sugrīva, lord of monkeys, be disregarded by you; he is grateful, capable of assuming any form at will, desirous of allies, and valiant.

sanskrit: śaktau hy adya yuvāṃ kartuṃ kāryaṃ tasya cikīrṣitam kṛtārtho vākṛtārtho vā kṛtyaṃ tava kariṣyati
english: For you two are now able to accomplish what he desires to do; and whether his own purpose is fulfilled or not, he will accomplish your task.

sanskrit: sa ṛkṣarajasaḥ putraḥ pampām aṭati śaṅkitaḥ bhāskarasyaurasaḥ putro vālinā kṛtakilbiṣaḥ
english: He, son of Ṛkṣaraja and natural son of Bhāskara, wanders about Pampā in fear, wronged by Vālin.

sanskrit: saṃnidhāyāyudhaṃ kṣipram ṛṣyamūkālayaṃ kapim kuru rāghava satyena vayasyaṃ vanacāriṇam
english: Having set aside your weapons, quickly make the monkey who dwells on Ṛśyamūka your sworn companion in truth, O Rāghava, that forest-wanderer.

sanskrit: sa hi sthānāni sarvāṇi kārtsnyena kapikuñjaraḥ naramāṃsāśināṃ loke naipuṇyād adhigacchati
english: For that elephant among monkeys in his entirety, by his skill, reaches all the haunts in the world of those who eat human flesh.

sanskrit: na tasyāviditaṃ loke kiṃ cid asti hi rāghava yāvat sūryaḥ pratapati sahasrāṃśur ariṃdama
english: Nothing whatsoever in the world is unknown to him, O Rāghava, as far as the thousand-rayed Sūrya blazes, O subduer of enemies.

sanskrit: sa nadīr vipulāñ śailān giridurgāṇi kandarān anviṣya vānaraiḥ sārdhaṃ patnīṃ te 'dhigamiṣyati
english: He, searching great rivers, mountains, mountain-strongholds, and caves together with his monkeys, will discover your wife.

sanskrit: vānarāṃś ca mahākāyān preṣayiṣyati rāghava diśo vicetuṃ tāṃ sītāṃ tvadviyogena śocatīm
english: And he will send out mighty-bodied monkeys in every direction, O Rāghava, to search for that Sītā who grieves in separation from you.

sanskrit: sa meruśṛṅgāgragatām aninditāṃ praviśya pātālatale 'pi vāśritām plavaṃgamānāṃ pravaras tava priyāṃ nihatya rakṣāṃsi punaḥ pradāsyati
english: That foremost of leaping ones will restore your beloved to you — even if she has gone to the peak of Meru, or taken refuge at the floor of the netherworld — entering even there and slaying the rākṣasas.

sanskrit: nidarśayitvā rāmāya sītāyāḥ pratipādane vākyam anvartham arthajñaḥ kabandhaḥ punar abravīt
english: Having thus shown Rāma the way to recover Sītā in words pregnant with meaning, Kabandha, knower of purposes, spoke again:

sanskrit: eṣa rāma śivaḥ panthā yatraite puṣpitā drumāḥ pratīcīṃ diśam āśritya prakāśante manoramāḥ
english: "This, O Rāma, is the auspicious path where these flowering trees, stretching toward the western direction, shine forth in delightful beauty.

sanskrit: jambūpriyālapanasāḥ plakṣanyagrodhatindukāḥ aśvatthāḥ karṇikārāś ca cūtāś cānye ca pādapāḥ
english: Jambū, priyāla, panasa, plakṣa, nyagrodha, tinduka, aśvattha, karṇikāra, cūta, and other trees as well —

sanskrit: tān āruhyātha vā bhūmau pātayitvā ca tān balāt phalāny amṛtakalpāni bhakṣayantau gamiṣyathaḥ
english: climbing them or felling them to the ground by force, you two shall go on eating fruits that rival ambrosia.

sanskrit: caṅkramantau varān deśāñ śailāc chailaṃ vanād vanam tataḥ puṣkariṇīṃ vīrau pampāṃ nāma gamiṣyathaḥ
english: Roaming through fine regions, from mountain to mountain, from forest to forest, you two heroes shall then reach the lake and pool called Pampā.

sanskrit: aśarkarām avibhraṃśāṃ samatīrtham aśaivalām rāma saṃjātavālūkāṃ kamalotpalaśobhitām
english: O Rāma, it is without pebbles, without slipperiness, with even banks, free from algae, with sandy shores newly formed, beautified with lotuses and water-lilies.

sanskrit: tatra haṃsāḥ plavāḥ krauñcāḥ kurarāś caiva rāghava valgusvarā nikūjanti pampāsalilagocarāḥ
english: There, O Rāghava, swans, waterbirds, cranes, and osprey — dwelling in the waters of Pampā — cry out melodiously.

sanskrit: nodvijante narān dṛṣṭvā vadhasyākovidāḥ śubhāḥ ghṛtapiṇḍopamān sthūlāṃs tān dvijān bhakṣayiṣyathaḥ
english: Those beautiful birds, unversed in slaughter and untroubled at the sight of men, you two shall feast upon — those plump birds resembling lumps of clarified butter.

sanskrit: rohitān vakratuṇḍāṃś ca nalamīnāṃś ca rāghava pampāyām iṣubhir matsyāṃs tatra rāma varān hatān
english: Rohita fish, crooked-mouthed fish, and reed-fish, O Rāghava — choice fish struck with arrows there in Pampā, O Rāma —

sanskrit: nistvakpakṣān ayastaptān akṛśān ekakaṇṭakān tava bhaktyā samāyukto lakṣmaṇaḥ saṃpradāsyati
english: — those skinned, scaled, iron-roasted, plump, single-boned ones, Lakṣmaṇa, joined in devotion to you, shall offer you.

sanskrit: bhṛśaṃ te khādato matsyān pampāyāḥ puṣpasaṃcaye padmagandhi śivaṃ vāri sukhaśītam anāmayam
english: As you eagerly eat the fish amid the cluster of blooms of Pampā, Lakṣmaṇa shall give you to drink the auspicious water fragrant with lotuses, pleasantly cool and wholesome.

sanskrit: uddhṛtya sa tadākliṣṭaṃ rūpyasphaṭikasaṃnibham atha puṣkaraparṇena lakṣmaṇaḥ pāyayiṣyati
english: Drawing it up fresh and unstained, resembling silver and crystal, Lakṣmaṇa shall then give you to drink using a lotus leaf.

sanskrit: sthūlān giriguhāśayyān varāhān vanacāriṇaḥ apāṃ lobhād upāvṛttān vṛṣabhān iva nardataḥ rūpānvitāṃś ca pampāyāṃ drakṣyasi tvaṃ narottama
english: Plump boars sleeping in mountain caves, forest-wanderers returning out of greed for water, roaring like bulls, handsome in form — these you shall see at Pampā, O best of men.

sanskrit: sāyāhne vicaran rāma viṭapī mālyadhāriṇaḥ śītodakaṃ ca pampāyāṃ dṛṣṭvā śokaṃ vihāsyasi
english: At evening, roaming about, O Rāma, seeing the flowering trees adorned with garlands and the cool water of Pampā, you shall cast off your grief.

sanskrit: sumanobhiś citāṃs tatra tilakān naktamālakān utpalāni ca phullāni paṅkajāni ca rāghava
english: There the tilaka and naktamāla trees are painted with blossoms, and the utpala and paṅkaja lotus-flowers are in full bloom, O Rāghava.

sanskrit: na tāni kaś cin mālyāni tatrāropayitā naraḥ mataṅgaśiṣyās tatrāsann ṛṣayaḥ susamāhitaḥ
english: No man will have strung those garlands there; the sages who were disciples of Mataṅga dwelt there, supremely concentrated.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ bhārābhitaptānāṃ vanyam āharatāṃ guroḥ ye prapetur mahīṃ tūrṇaṃ śarīrāt svedabindavaḥ
english: From those who were wearied by their burdens and brought forest produce for their teacher, the beads of sweat that fell swiftly to the earth from their bodies —

sanskrit: tāni mālyāni jātāni munīnāṃ tapasā tadā svedabindusamutthāni na vinaśyanti rāghava
english: — from those have these garlands been born, arising from the beads of sweat, through the austerity of the sages in that time; they perish not, O Rāghava.

sanskrit: teṣām adyāpi tatraiva dṛśyate paricāriṇī śramaṇī śabarī nāma kākutstha cirajīvinī
english: Even to this day there is seen serving them in that very place an ascetic woman named Śabarī, O descendant of Kākutstha, long-lived.

sanskrit: tvāṃ tu dharme sthitā nityaṃ sarvabhūtanamaskṛtam dṛṣṭvā devopamaṃ rāma svargalokaṃ gamiṣyati
english: Steadfast ever in righteousness, revered by all beings, she, upon seeing you, O Rāma, who are like a god, shall depart for the heavenly world.

sanskrit: tatas tad rāma pampāyās tīram āśritya paścimam āśramasthānam atulaṃ guhyaṃ kākutstha paśyasi
english: Then, O Rāma, taking shelter on the western bank of Pampā, you shall see that hermitage, incomparable and secret, O descendant of Kākutstha.

sanskrit: na tatrākramituṃ nāgāḥ śaknuvanti tam āśramam ṛṣes tasya mataṅgasya vidhānāt tac ca kānanam
english: Not even elephants are able to enter that hermitage, by the ordinance of that sage Mataṅga, nor can they enter that forest grove.

sanskrit: tasmin nandanasaṃkāśe devāraṇyopame vane nānāvihagasaṃkīrṇe raṃsyase rāma nirvṛtaḥ
english: In that forest resembling Nandana, like the divine grove, filled with diverse birds, you shall delight, O Rāma, at peace.

sanskrit: ṛṣyamūkas tu pampāyāḥ purastāt puṣpitadrumaḥ suduḥkhārohaṇo nāma śiśunāgābhirakṣitaḥ udāro brahmaṇā caiva pūrvakāle vinirmitaḥ
english: To the east of Pampā stands Ṛśyamūka, covered with flowering trees, very difficult to ascend, guarded by young elephants, and magnanimously fashioned by Brahmā in ancient time.

sanskrit: śayānaḥ puruṣo rāma tasya śailasya mūrdhani yat svapne labhate vittaṃ tat prabuddho 'dhigacchati
english: O Rāma, a man sleeping on the summit of that mountain — whatever wealth he obtains in a dream, that he obtains upon waking.

sanskrit: na tv enaṃ viṣamācāraḥ pāpakarmādhirohati tatraiva praharanty enaṃ suptam ādāya rākṣasāḥ
english: But a man of crooked conduct and evil deeds cannot ascend it; the rākṣasas there seize him as he sleeps and strike him down.

sanskrit: tato 'pi śiśunāgānām ākrandaḥ śrūyate mahān krīḍatāṃ rāma pampāyāṃ mataṅgāraṇyavāsinām
english: From there too a great cry of young elephants is heard, O Rāma — those who sport in Pampā, dwelling in the Mataṅga forest.

sanskrit: siktā rudhiradhārābhiḥ saṃhatya paramadvipāḥ pracaranti pṛthak kīrṇā meghavarṇās tarasvinaḥ
english: Wetted with streams of blood from fighting together, those supreme elephants, cloud-colored and swift, roam about scattered in different directions.

sanskrit: te tatra pītvā pānīyaṃ vimalaṃ śītam avyayam nivṛttāḥ saṃvigāhante vanāni vanagocarāḥ
english: Having drunk the pure, cool, and inexhaustible water there, those forest-dwelling ones turn back and plunge into the forests.

sanskrit: rāma tasya tu śailasya mahatī śobhate guhā śilāpidhānā kākutstha duḥkhaṃ cāsyāḥ praveśanam
english: O Rāma, there shines on that mountain a great cave, sealed by a boulder, O descendant of Kākutstha, and entry into it is difficult.

sanskrit: tasyā guhāyāḥ prāgdvāre mahāñ śītodako hradaḥ bahumūlaphalo ramyo nānānagasamāvṛtaḥ
english: Before the eastern entrance of that cave lies a great pool of cool water, delightful, rich in roots and fruits, surrounded by diverse trees.

sanskrit: tasyāṃ vasati sugrīvaś caturbhiḥ saha vānaraiḥ kadā cic chikhare tasya parvatasyāvatiṣṭhate
english: In that cave dwells Sugrīva together with four monkeys; at times he stands upon the peak of that mountain.

sanskrit: kabandhas tv anuśāsyaivaṃ tāv ubhau rāmalakṣmaṇau sragvī bhāskaravarṇābhaḥ khe vyarocata vīryavān
english: Having thus instructed both Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, Kabandha — wearing a garland, radiant as the color of the sun, full of valor — shone in the sky.

sanskrit: taṃ tu khasthaṃ mahābhāgaṃ kabandhaṃ rāmalakṣmaṇau prasthitau tvaṃ vrajasveti vākyam ūcatur antikāt
english: Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, about to depart, addressed that illustrious Kabandha standing in the sky from nearby: "Go now."

sanskrit: gamyatāṃ kāryasiddhyartham iti tāv abravīc ca saḥ suprītau tāv anujñāpya kabandhaḥ prasthitas tadā
english: "May you go for the accomplishment of your purpose" — thus he spoke to those two; and having given leave to those two who were supremely pleased, Kabandha departed then.

sanskrit: sa tat kabandhaḥ pratipadya rūpaṃ vṛtaḥ śriyā bhāskaratulyadehaḥ nidarśayan rāmam avekṣya khasthaḥ sakhyaṃ kuruṣveti tadābhyuvāca
english: That Kabandha, having recovered his form, endowed with splendor, his body equal to the sun, standing in the sky and showing himself, looked upon Rāma and then spoke: "Make alliance."
